title: "Batch"
description: "A group of examples processed together during a model or data-processing operation."
term: "Batch"
letter: "B"
category: "Deep Learning"
difficulty: "Beginner"
---

## Simple explanation

A batch is a group of examples handled together. For model training, a batch
lets the system calculate predictions and learning signals for several
examples in one operation.

## Technical explanation

In mini-batch training, the training set is divided into batches. The model
computes a loss over a batch and uses its gradient to update parameters.
Batching can also refer to grouping requests in an inference service or
grouping records in a data-processing pipeline.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Batching can improve hardware utilization and throughput, but it affects
memory use, latency, and sometimes the statistical properties of training.
Its meaning should be clear from context: training batches and inference
request batches serve different operational purposes.

## How it works

The system collects a set of examples, combines or vectorizes their
operations, and processes them together. For a training batch $B$, a common
objective is the mean loss:

$$
L_B = \frac{1}{|B|}\sum_{i \in B} \ell_i
$$

The optimizer updates model parameters using the gradient of $L_B$.

## Practical example

Instead of sending one image at a time through a classifier during
training, a data loader can provide a batch of 32 images, provided that
the model and available device memory support that size.

## Common misconceptions

- A batch is not necessarily the entire dataset.
- A larger batch does not automatically produce a better model.
- In inference systems, batching can increase throughput while increasing
  the wait time for an individual request.
